title: General Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte — General Order dated November 20, 2026 revises the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure, section 2-Parties, including to require funding disclosures for Intervenors. This matter was decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.

LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                    GENERAL ORDER NUMBER 11-20-2026 (R-36241)

               LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION, EX PARTE

Docket No. R-36241, In re: Rulemaking to Revise the Commission's Rules of Practice and
Procedure.

               (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


OVERVIEW AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY

       This rulemaking was initiated in January 2022 as a result of Louisiana Public Service

Commission (“LPSC” or “Commission”) recognition that the Commission’s Rules of Practice and

Procedure (“Rules”) needed a review, and possible revisions, as they had not been updated in

approximately 20 years. Since that time, Staff has been working to review and substantially revise

the Rules to not only clarify specific components, but also to ensure the Rules are up-to-date.

       In response to the Notice of Proceeding filed by Commission Staff, which was published

in the Commission’s Official Bulletin dated January 7, 2022, timely notices to intervene were filed

by: Louisiana Energy Users Group (“LEUG”); Alliance for Affordable Energy (“AAE”);

Southwestern Electric Power Company (“SWEPCO”); Cabot Corporation (“Cabot”); Entergy

Louisiana, LLC (“ELL”); Cleco Power (“Cleco Power”); CenterPoint Energy Resources Corp.

(“CNP”). The Internet and Television Association (“LCTA”) filed for interested party status, and

a motion for intervention out of time was filed by Association of Louisiana Electric Cooperatives,

Inc. (“ALEC”), which was granted.

       At the Commission’s April 15, 2026 Business and Executive (“B&E”) Session, the

Commission directed Staff to implement an interim Rule 10a for mandatory disclosure of foreign

and outside funding sources by Intervenors in Commission proceedings. Specifically, Staff was

directed to:

       [P]repare, for consideration at the earliest practicable B&E, but no later than June,
       a proposed Interim Rule 10a, or other appropriate placement in the Commission’s
       Rules of Practice and Procedure, that would require all Intervenors in every docket,
       proceeding, or matter before the Commission to publicly disclose and certify all
       sources of funding for their organization that originate, directly or indirectly, from
       individuals or entities located outside of Louisiana, including without limitation the
       following foreign nations: the People’s Republic of China (PRC), the Democratic
       People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK), the Russian Federation, and the Islamic
       Republic of Iran (or any entities, agents, or intermediaries controlled by or
       substantially funded by those governments). The proposed rule shall apply to both
       existing and future Intervenors and shall include, at a minimum:




                                                        General Order No. 11-20-2026 (R-36241)
                                                                                        Page 1
               A requirement for a sworn affidavit or certification filed with every
          intervention pleading (and updated annually or upon any material change in
          funding);
              A statement of the percentage of annual funding from individuals or
          entities located or domiciled outside the state of Louisiana;
              Full disclosure of any grants, donations, contracts, or other financial
          support received, directly or indirectly, from the listed foreign nations or their
          state-linked entities during the preceding five (5) years;
             Identification of the ultimate source(s) of funds, including any pass-
          through foundations, nonprofits, or intermediaries;
              Public filing of the disclosure in the docket (subject to any narrowly
          tailored protections for truly proprietary non-funding information);
              A clear statement that failure to comply may result in denial or revocation
          of Intervenor status, sanctions, or other remedies as determined by the
          Commission; and
             An effective date no later than sixty (60) days after adoption of any
          proposed rule.
       Staff shall model this proposed disclosure requirement rule on analogous
       transparency provisions in Louisiana law (e.g., recent third-party litigation funding
       disclosure statutes) while tailoring the Commission’s rule to the administrative
       context of Commission proceedings. Further, any proposed rule should emphasize
       that this is a transparency measure to protect the integrity of the Commission’s
       regulatory process, Louisiana ratepayers, and the public interest, not a bar to
       participation.

       In proposing an Interim Rule pursuant to this directive, Staff shall also include any
       such proposed rule within Staff’s proposed revisions to the Commission’s Rules of
       Practice and Procedure currently being reviewed in Docket No. R-36241 in order
       to allow stakeholder comment.

       This Directive is issued in furtherance of the Commission’s mission and the broader
       goal of achieving Louisiana Energy Dominance.

As a result of this Directive, several new parties filed motions to intervene out of time, which were

granted. Those parties were: Southern Energy Renewable Energy Association (“SERA”)

Environmental Defense Fund (“EDF”); Sierra Club; 1803 Electric Cooperative, Inc. (“1803”);

Delta Utilities; and CTIA – The Wireless Association (“CTIA”).

   While Staff is still working on a complete revision of the Rules, given the Commission’s

Directive at the April 2026 B&E, Staff began working on proposed rules associated with funding

disclosures for stakeholder input. As Staff’s review began, it became clear that the entire section

– Part II Parties – needed to be revised to portray the Commission’s long-standing policies related

to the various parties within Commission proceedings. As such, Staff filed its Notice of Proposed

Rules for Part 2-Parties on May 22, 2026 seeking comments thereon, which included proposed

revisions to the entire section related to parties in Commission proceedings (“May 26, 2026

Proposed Rules”). Comments were timely filed by: SWEPCO, ELL, AAE, EDF, CTIA, ALEC,



                                                        General Order No. 11-20-2026 (R-36241)
                                                                                        Page 2
 Cleco Power, SREA, LEUG, and Sierra Club. 1

    Generally, the jurisdictional electric utilities were supportive of the May 22, 2026 Proposed

Rules; however, all provided comments that jurisdictional utilities should be exempt from the

funding disclosure requirement as the Commission is already privy to the respective utility’s

financial information. LEUG initially expressed concerns with the May 22, 2026 Proposed Rules

pertaining to respective roles and levels of participation in Commission proceedings, and provided

proposed redlines to address those concerns. EDF’s comments provided areas that could use

clarification and revisions to ensure the proposed rules do not inadvertently curtail public input

and participation. CTIA, Sierra Club, and SERA commented that the May 22, 2026 Proposed

Rules were unduly burdensome and raised constitutional concerns. AAE also provided comments

focused on legal and practical concerns resulting from the proposed rules.

    After reviewing all comments filed, Staff filed its second Notice of Proposed Rules for Part 2

– “Parties” on July 27, 2026 providing a revised proposed rule that addressed a majority of the

comments, and requests for clarifications, filed in response to Staff’s May 22, 2026 Proposed Rules

(“July 27, 2026 Proposed Rules”). Comments on the July 27, 2026 Proposed Rules were timely

filed by: Cleco Power; CTIA; 1803; EDF; ELL; SWEPCO; AAE; Sierra Club; ALEC; LEUG;

and the Pelican Institute for Public Policy (“Pelican Institute”).2 While ELL, SWEPCO, LEUG,

and CTIA all provided comments indicating no additional revisions were necessary to the July 27,

2026 Proposed Rules, Cleco Power maintained its position that all jurisdictional utilities should be

exempt from the proposed funding disclosure rules, now contained in proposed Rule 11. AAE,

ALEC, and 1803 all provided suggested modifications and clarifications, and EDF, Sierra Club,

and the Pelican Institute maintained that the July 27, 2026 Proposed Rules did not overcome

constitutional barriers related to freedom of association.

    Staff filed its third set of proposed rules on September 9, 2026 titled Staff’s Final Proposed

Rules for Part 2 – “Parties,” providing notice to all Intervenors that this was the final review of

proposed rules and requested comments thereon (“September 9, 2026 Proposed Rules”). The

September 9, 2026 Proposed Rules made substantial changes based upon comments received in

response to the July 27, 2026 Proposed Rules, including limiting disclosure requirements to foreign

 adversaries as defined in 15 C.F.R. 7.4, as well as secondary/tertiary funding from the same.

Comments were timely filed by: ALEC; 1803; Cleco Power; SWEPCO; ELL; AAE; LEUG;

SREA; Sierra Club; and the Pelican Institute. 1803, Cleco Power, and SWEPCO all provided

comments indicating no additional edits were necessary. Generally, ALEC, ELL, AAE, LEUG,

and SERA all indicated that they had no major concerns; however, each had comments suggesting

slight modifications to the September 9, 2026 Proposed Rules. Sierra Club and the Pelican Institute

indicated substantive revisions were still necessary. Sierra Club and the Pelican Institute continued

to comment that the proposed rules were broad sweeping and not narrowly tailored, and requested

additional narrowing of the September 9, 2026 Proposed Rules.

    Staff took these additional comments into consideration and issued Notice of Final Proposed

Rules for Part 2 – Parties on October 7, 2026 (“Final Proposed Rules”), which were considered at

the Commission’s October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session, and attached hereto as

Attachment A.3


COMMISSION JURISDICTION

         Article IV, Section 21 (B) of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974 grants the LPSC

constitutional jurisdiction over common carriers, and specifically provides as follows:

         “The [public service] commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
         utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law. It shall adopt
         and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and procedures necessary for the
         discharge of its duties, and shall have other powers and perform other duties as
         provided by law.”

The Commission’s power is as complete in every respect as the regulatory power that would have

been vested in the legislature absent Article IV, Section 21. Consequently, “the Commission is

vested explicitly and implicitly with the constitutional power necessary to the performance of its

function of regulating common carriers and public utilities through the adoption and enforcement

of reasonable rules and orders requisite to these purposes.” Louisiana Consumers’ League Inc. v.

LPSC, 351 So.2d 128, 131 (La. 1977); Central Louisiana Electric Co. v. LPSC, 373 So. 2d 123,

128 (La. 1979); South Central Bell Telephone Co. v. LPSC, 412 So. 2d 1069, 1070 (La. 1982).




OVERVIEW OF PART 2 REVISIONS




3 Upon issuance of this General Order, the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure will be updated to reflect

the revisions approved herein for Part 2 – Parties.

                                                                General Order No. 11-20-2026 (R-36241)
                                                                                                Page 4
     Throughout this rulemaking process, and as evident in the attached rules hereto, the majority

of changes to Rules 9-10 codify the Commission’s long-standing practice for the various parties

in Commission proceedings. The substantive changes contained in the Final Proposed Rules relate

to the funding disclosure requirement for Intervenors, which is now codified in Rule 11.

    As indicated in the Commission’s April 15, 2026 Directive, the goal of a funding disclosure

requirement is to further the Commission’s mission to impartially, equitably, and efficiently

regulate the rates and services of public utilities and common carriers within Louisiana, as well as

strive to maintain existing business and industry, promote economic development, and protect

consumers within the state. The Commission’s directive also indicated the purpose of the funding

disclosure requirement was for the broader goal of achieving Louisiana energy dominance. The

Commission’s directive was based upon a finding that participation in Commission dockets by

entities whose funding is directed, controlled, or substantially influenced by a foreign country of

concern, as defined in 15 C.F.R. § 7.4, or by an entity acting on behalf of such a foreign country,

can undermine the integrity of Commission proceeding affecting Louisiana ratepayers, energy

infrastructure, and the public interest. Such findings were drawn from the Pelican Institute for

Public Policy’s March 2026 report, Barriers to Louisiana Energy Dominance, which documented

organizations having received over $100 million in out-of-state funding since 2020,4 including

millions in combined grants from the U.S. Energy Foundation and Energy Foundation China.5

Concerning to the Commission was the report that Energy Foundation China has faced intense

scrutiny over allegations of Chinese Communist Party connections and improper foreign influence,

including funneling money to U.S.-based organizations to advance Chinese energy policies.6

    Transparency of underlying goals and policies in Commission proceeding assist the

Commission in understanding the various interests and/or biases of all parties providing relevant

information in a proceeding – both proponents and opponents. The Final Proposed Rules provide

the terms on which all parties may participate as intervenors in Commission proceedings, with

Rule 11 governing the terms on which intervenors may participate in Commission proceedings.

The Final Proposed Rules do not purport to regulate the internal affairs, governance, or operations

of any intervenor beyond what is necessary to administer intervention in Commission proceedings.

COMMISSION CONSIDERATION

    This matter was considered by the Commission at the October 22, 2026 Business and

Executive Session. After discussion, on motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice

Chairman Coussan, and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to adopt the Final Proposed

Rules filed into the record on October 7, 2026.

IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED THAT:

       1) The Commission’s adopts Staff’s Final Rules filed into the record on October 7, 2026,
          attached hereto as Attachment A.

       2) This order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION

                                           PART II PARTIES

RULE 9:        CLASSIFICATION OF PARTIES.

A party to proceedings before the Louisiana Public Service Commission are applicants,
complainants, respondents, or intervenors. Classification as a party allows full participation in a
Commission proceeding, including procedural or substantive rights authorized by the
Commission. As defined below, the Commission also recognizes a classification of Interested
Party, which are not considered a party to a Commission proceeding, but can be placed on the
Commission’s Official Service List to monitor any Commission proceeding. Regardless of errors
in their designation of themselves in their pleadings, the Commission may align parties in
accordance with their interest in the proceedings.

       Applicant, is an individual or an entity commencing a proceeding before the
       Commission with an application as the initiating filing seeking the Commission’s
       approval, acceptance, or non-opposition.

       Complainant is an individual or an entity commencing a proceeding before the
       Commission with a complaint as the initiating document seeking the Commission
       require a refund, assess a fine, or otherwise rectify an issue.

       Interested Party is an individual or an entity who desires to monitor a proceeding
       before the Commission. Upon the filing of a Notice for Interested Party Status, such
       individual(s) will be classified as an Interested Party and placed on the official
       Service List of said proceeding for proceeding notifications issued by the
       Commission and to receive service of publicly filed versions of pleadings and
       testimony. Interested Party classification differs from other party classifications in
       that an Interested Party does not enjoy the benefits of full participation in the
       proceeding as if the individual or entity was an applicant, complainant, intervenor,
       or respondent. An Interested Party shall not have discovery rights or obligations,
       including the receipt of data requests and responses thereto, submit testimony or
       briefs, or participate in hearings before an Administrative Law Judge.

       Intervenor is an individual or entity actually in interest who timely files a Notice of
       Intervention in a proceeding indicating the interest in said proceeding, regardless if
       that interest is to support, oppose, or monitor the proceeding. Any party seeking to
       oppose a Notice of Intervention shall file a motion to strike pursuant the
       Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure.

       Respondent is a named public utility or common carrier against whom relief is
       sought in a complaint, citation, or other proceeding.

Any party, including civic and trade associations, actually in interest may file a notice to appear in
any proceeding before the Louisiana Public Service Commission on his/her own behalf or be
represented as provided for in Rule 10 below. All appearances shall be subject to a motion to
strike upon a showing that the party has no justiciable or administratively cognizable interest in
the proceeding.

Unless otherwise provided by law, any public official, agency or department of the State of
Louisiana or any of its political subdivisions shall be permitted to appear in any proceeding
whether as a formal intervenor or otherwise, and present any relevant and proper testimony and
evidence bearing upon the issues involved in the particular proceeding.

RULE 10:       APPEARANCES PERSONALLY OR BY REPRESENTATIVE.

Any party may appear and be represented by an attorney at law authorized to practice law before
the highest court of any State. A natural person may appear on his own behalf. A corporation,
partnership or association may appear and be represented by any bona fide officer, partner, full-
time employee, or other person if authorized to so appear by the Commission.

No party may have more than six representatives on a service list for any given Commission
proceeding. If good cause exists for an entity to have more than six representatives on a service

                                                         General Order No. 11-20-2026 (R-36241)
                                                                                         Page 8
 list, such request must be provided in writing to the Commission’s Records Division, who will
accept or reject the request.

The Commission, and its Staff, shall be considered a party to every docketed proceeding without
the necessity of filing for intervention, with the Commission’s Legal Division being the designated
representative for the Commission.

RULE 11: INTERVENOR’S DISCLOSURE OF FUNDING SOURCES

Any party who wishes to intervene in a Commission proceeding shall first, or at least concurrently
with a Notice for Intervention, file an Intervenor Disclosure of Funding Sources with the
Commission in the Commission’s Funding Disclosure Repository Docket.

The Intervenor Disclosure of Funding Sources shall include:
       1) A certification either by the party, or by a representative of, affirming:
              a. The authenticity of the information provided after a reasonable inquiry by the
                  Intervenor;
              b. Whether the Intervenor is a Foreign Adversary, an Agent(s) of a Foreign
                  Adversary, serves as a corporate officer of, board director of, or limited liability
                  company manager of, a Foreign Adversary or an Agent of a Foreign Adversary,
                  or has an ownership interest in a Foreign Adversary or an Agent(s) of a Foreign
                  Adversary as those terms are defined below;
              c. Whether the Intervenor currently owes debt in excess of $50,000 in the
                  aggregate to a Foreign Adversary or to an Agent(s) of Foreign Adversaries; and
              d. Whether the Intervenor has made other disclosures under the “Transparency
                  and Limitations on Foreign Third-Party Litigation Funding Act” or to the
                  Louisiana Board of Ethics as a lobbyist for a foreign adversary in accordance
                  with La. R.S. 24:53.1

       2) Disclosure of funding sources shall include contributions received from a Foreign
          Adversary, an Agent(s) of a Foreign Adversary, and Secondary/Tertiary Funding, as
          defined below, for the prior twelve calendar (12) months that total in the aggregate
          more than $5,000 or 5% of total contributions to the Intervenor.
              a. For contributions received from a Foreign Adversary or an Agent(s) of a
                 Foreign Adversary, the disclosure shall include a list of each contributor, the
                 date of each contribution, the amount of each contribution, and the purpose of
                 each contribution.
              b. For all Secondary or Tertiary Funding received, the disclosure shall include a
                 list of each contributor, the date of each contribution, the amount of each
                 contribution, the purpose of each contribution, and a description of the
                 intermediary through which the contributions passed, including the identity and
                 when the contribution passed.

Intervenors shall take reasonable efforts to determine if any Funding originates from a Foreign
Adversary, an Agent(s) of a Foreign Adversary, or through Secondary/Tertiary Funding. If, after
reasonable inquiry, no contribution is identified as being received from a Foreign Adversary, an
Agent(s) of a Foreign Adversary, or via Secondary/Tertiary Funding, a certification made by the
Intervenor, or an authorized representative of the Intervenor, to that effect is required.

“Reasonable inquiry” for determining whether contributions originate from a Foreign Adversary,
an Agent(s) of a Foreign Adversary, or via Secondary/Tertiary Funding, does not require an
Intervenor to investigate or otherwise research the citizenship, residency, ownership, financial
sources, or other background of each individual contributor in order to determine whether, and
certify that, the Intervenor has not received Foreign Adversary or Secondary/Tertiary Funding.

Foreign Adversary is a natural person, a juridical person, or a foreign government listed in 15
C.F.R. § 7.4 (or any successor regulation). This definition shall include any juridical person or
entity that is owned or controlled by the government of a foreign country of concern, or a
partnership, association, corporation, organization or other combination of person organized under
the law of or having its principal place of business in a foreign country of concern, or a subsidiary
of such entity.


                                                         General Order No. 11-20-2026 (R-36241)
                                                                                         Page 9
 Agent(s) of Foreign Adversary is a person that serves as agent for a principal of a Foreign
Adversary; is under the direction of a Foreign Adversary that has the power to direct or cause the
direction of the management or policies of a juridical person, whether through a controlling
interest, contract, or otherwise; has a controlling interest in a juridical person; or is a juridical
person that is organized under the laws of, headquartered in, or has its principal place of business
in a country identified as a Foreign Adversary.

Controlling Interest is possession of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management
or policies of a juridical person. A person or entity that directly or indirectly has the right to vote
fifty percent or more of the voting interest of juridical person or is entitled to fifty percent or more
of its profits or distributions is presumed to possess a controlling interest.

Secondary/Tertiary Funding is a contribution or other transfer of value that originates from a
Foreign Adversary or an Agent(s) of a Foreign Adversary and is received by the Intervenor
indirectly through one or more intermediary organizations, foundations, corporations, fiscal
sponsors, or other third parties.

Disclosure obligations under Rule 11 shall apply to contributions received on or after the effective
date of this Rule, and shall remain during the pendency of any Commission proceeding where a
party is considered an Intervenor. As such, all Intervenors shall ensure its respective Intervenor
Disclosure of Funding Sources is accurate at all times, and shall file an updated disclosure by
March 31st of each year for the preceding calendar year in the Commission’s Funding Disclosure
Repository Docket. Filing an updated disclosure with the Commission by March 31st of each year
satisfies the compliance obligation included herein for all Commission proceedings an Intervenor
is currently a party to, as well as any new proceedings an Intervenor elects to participate in during
that calendar year.

Such disclosure shall be publicly filed, subject to narrowly tailored protections for proprietary
non-funding information. The Commission reserves it right to review any claimed confidential
information and object to the same.

Failure of any Intervenor to provide the requisite funding disclosure may result in Commission
denial, or revocation, of Intervenor status in the relevant Commission proceeding(s), after
Commission notice of any deficiencies and the opportunity for the Intervenor to correct said
deficiency.
